page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 252 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, the system provides 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes an L3 cache of 32 MB, L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and L1d cache of 48 KB. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 variants) and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4d-highmem-32 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-core performance is also strong, with Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 10% and PassMark CPU scores in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform in the top 10%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls in the top 25%. Memory performance is solid, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25%, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidth benchmarks sit in the middle 50%. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small LLM models and strong static web serving throughput, while database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highmem-32 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 7.88 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of higher vCPU counts. The dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance make it well-suited for memory-intensive applications, software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. It is also highly capable for running small-scale LLM inference and high-throughput static web serving, though workloads requiring massive local storage or GPU acceleration will require external attachments or alternative instance types.
